thread:
mika (CS): FYI ParcelX onboarding — they're seeing intermittent 403s from the Node SDK after we enabled their edge proxy. Account flagged for health check, they mentioned renewal timeline next month. Can someone help?

jason (eng): Can you paste a minimal repro + logs? 403 could be auth or client-id mismatch.

mika (CS): Repro steps from ParcelX: 1) init SDK in Lambda 2) call /v1/generate 3) sometimes returns 200, sometimes 403. Logs: 

parcelx-onboard-bot: [2026-02-14T15:12:02Z] request id=aa12 auth=ok status=200
parcelx-onboard-bot: [2026-02-14T15:12:05Z] request id=aa13 auth=missing-header status=403 

mika (CS): Their SDK init (snippet):
```js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-x', prompt: 'hi' });
```

mika (CS): They use an internal edge that does a 307 to a regional gateway. They suspect nothing changed on their side.

olga (support-engineer): @mika can you confirm whether the 403 payload contains any error code? e.g., "invalid_client_id" vs "missing_authorization"? often useful to triage.

mika (CS): Payloads vary, here's one: 
```json
{"error":"unauthorized","reason":"Authorization header missing after redirect"}
```

jason (eng): Ah — classic redirect auth-drop. Many HTTP clients drop Authorization on 3xx->redirect. Which HTTP client is the SDK using?

olga (support-engineer): Node SDK uses node-fetch under the hood with default redirect: 'follow' which will drop auth for cross-host redirects. If their edge returns 307 -> different host, header can be removed by fetch.

jason (eng): Quick repro: run curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer x" https://edge.example/redirect -> observe Authorization not forwarded.

mika (CS): ParcelX says they see the pattern: first warmup requests succeed (same host), later requests routed to a regional host -> 403. They hit renewals slack today. Not yet escalated to legal but renewal at risk if unresolved quickly.

olga (support-engineer): Short-term workaround for them: set the SDK env var to use redirect=manual so the client follows the Location and re-adds Auth, or configure their edge to preserve Authorization on internal redirects. Example: set REDWOOD_HTTP_REDIRECT=manual (SDK accepts this flag for debugging).

jason (eng): Longer-term: we'll add logic to reapply Authorization on cross-host redirects in Node SDK or switch to fetch with redirect:'manual' and perform explicit second request with headers. I'll open a tiny patch.

mika (CS): ParcelX asked for config snippets. I suggested two options:
1) Edge change (preferred): ensure internal 307 keeps Authorization. For nginx: `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;`
2) SDK workaround: set env to force manual redirect and retry with headers. Sample snippet:
```js
process.env.REDWOOD_HTTP_REDIRECT = 'manual';
// client will return redirect response so you can re-issue with same auth
```

jason (eng): Patch created: GH #4821 — Node SDK: preserve auth on cross-host redirect or fall back to manual redirect flow. Small risk but test coverage added.

olga (support-engineer): I asked ParcelX to try the nginx change first. They rolled it to staging and reported no 403s in ~30m.

mika (CS): ParcelX says staging looks stable, will deploy to prod tonight. They've pushed their renewal decision to next week pending prod run. I flagged CSM and renewal manager.

jason (eng): Will merge the SDK patch tomorrow and cut a patch release.

olga (support-engineer): I'll follow up tomorrow to confirm prod run and capture feedback for docs (onboarding note: redirect behavior & proxies).

mika (CS): Thanks all — adding note to account health: "Auth header dropped by edge redirect; nginx proxy_set_header fix applied; SDK patch pending; monitor prod rollout" :thumbsup: 

parcelx-onboard-bot: [2026-02-14T16:02:00Z] ParcelX-staging: no 403s observed in 1800s

mika (CS): Closing thread once prod green. If prod shows any more flakiness we will escalate to SRE for gateway routing change.
